svg.title: Agent Hands V1 trust boundaries: executor, verifier, reconciler, evidence
svg.desc: Four components with what each may and may not do. The executor and verifier are separate browser sessions; the reconciler is a pure function; every verdict is window attribution, not causal attribution.
svg.text: Legacy application (system of record)
MERIDIAN CORE — supplied external target, or the local look-alike fixture
exposes no API, no transaction id, no per-hold operator
Executor session
own interpreter, own browser context, operator A (supervisor)
MAY
• replay the human-signed mutating artifact
• issue requests the network allowlist permits
• log every non-GET it dispatches (kind = session | mutation)
MAY NOT
• retry a risky step, ever
• decide whether an unacknowledged mutation committed → UNRESOLVED
• resume at or before the consequential step after a handback
• call any model during replay (enforced by test)
Verifier session
fresh interpreter, fresh browser context, operator B (teller)
MAY
• replay a read-only artifact (member record page)
• issue GETs, plus POST to exactly /signon (authentication)
• return raw observations: status tokens + observed_at
MAY NOT
• send any other non-GET — aborted by ReadOnlyGuard, reported
• classify or interpret its own observation
• touch the executor's page, context or cookies
• read balances or names — status tokens only
Reconciler — pure function, no I/O
reconcile(expected, pre-image, post-image, executor result) → Reconciliation
MAY
• emit VERIFIED_COMMITTED · VERIFIED_NOT_COMMITTED · EFFECT_MISMATCH · UNVERIFIABLE
• stamp attribution = "window", both observed_at timestamps, window length, inputs_sha256
MAY NOT
• retry, act, or attribute the transition to this invocation; missing evidence is always UNVERIFIABLE
Evidence bundle (written by the orchestrator, read by anyone)
expected.json · pre.json · executor.json · post.json · reconciliation.json · manifest.json (artifact hashes, SHA-256 of every trace, verify_chain results) · hash-chained trace.jsonl
Stated bound: the chain is keyless — tamper-evident, not non-repudiable; truncating the tail is undetectable without an external anchor.
Not provided: credential independence — the demo's operators share one password and one privilege model the project does not control.
one consequential mutation (POST)
two read-only observations (pre, post)
executor result (masked,
success | unresolved | failure ...)
pre-image, post-image
(raw observations)
process + browser-context boundary: no shared page, cookies or memory
